What Few Investors Realize About QQQ’s Dividend

QQQ's dividend has grown roughly 75% over five years, yet its 0.43% yield generates only about $43 annually on a $10,000 position.

When top holdings like Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft raise their dividends, QQQ's distributions automatically grow without shareholders needing to act.

QQQ distributions are taxable whether reinvested or taken as cash, and net investment income is generally taxed as ordinary income.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Apple didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat AAPL. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

Almost nobody buys Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) for income. Even so, its dividend has grown about 75.0% over the past five years. Over roughly the same period, the fund's share price rose 87.4%, so the payout has kept close pace with the price.

QQQ's latest four quarterly distributions added up to $3.09182 per share. The four quarters ending September 2021 paid $1.76671. Plenty of retirees and near-retirees hold the Nasdaq-100 fund purely for growth, and many of them have a growing income stream they've never paid much attention to.

24/7 Wall St.
Where a $490 Billion Tech Fund Gets Its Dividend

QQQ had $490.1 billion in net assets as of June 30, 2026. Its prospectus sets out the payout rules: "Generally, dividends from net investment income, if any, are declared and paid quarterly by the Fund." The fund "also intends to distribute its net realized capital gains, if any, to shareholders annually."

Net investment income is simply what the fund collects in dividends and interest, minus its operating expenses. That means QQQ's payout depends entirely on what its holdings pay. The largest holdings as of June 30 include Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) at 7.6% of net assets, Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) at 6.7%, Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) at 4.4%, and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) at 4.0%.

title: Bitcoin and ETH Holders Could Face a Deeper Pullback, Ansem Warns
detail:
Bitcoin and ETH Holders Could Face a Deeper Pullback, Ansem Warns
Phil Haunhorst
Tue, October 27, 2026 at 12:38 AM MST 3 min read
BTC-USD
QQQ
ETH-USD
^NDX
Trade BTC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Photo by BeInCrypto

Crypto trader Ansem has turned bearish on Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH). He warns that both assets broke their mid-timeframe trend and could slide faster below $82,000 and $2,400.

Ansem also says being bullish onchain has become a contrarian position. In his view, sentiment is the worst he has seen in roughly nine years, and Bitcoin and ETH holders could face a deeper pullback.

Why Ansem Turned Bearish on Bitcoin Now

Ansem bases his call largely on stock market technicals. In his view, AI momentum stocks printed a parabolic blow-off top, a steep final surge that often marks the end of a rally. A lower high and a broken trend followed.

Meanwhile, he says even the largest tech names are stalling at all-time highs. He adds that a recent breakout in the Invesco QQQ, a fund that tracks the Nasdaq 100, has turned into a failed move above prior highs.

Ansem. Source: X

He also questions where the next wave of AI revenue will come from. He argues that heavy spending on model training has yet to lift profits in a meaningful way, and he points to Meta's post-earnings selloff as an example.

Headline risk adds more pressure. The Federal Reserve announces its rate decision on October 28, in a packed Fed week that also brings major earnings reports.

Crypto analyst Benjamin Cowen has also laid out a bearish Q4 roadmap for Bitcoin.

Bitcoin Price Performance. Source: BeInCrypto
Can Onchain Builders Lift the Mood?

Still, Ansem is not bearish on Bitcoin over the longer term. He expects a pullback first and then a move higher.

The crypto trader also expects heavy volatility in both directions through the fourth quarter. Even so, he believes parts of the onchain market could still do well.

Ansem saves his sharpest criticism for Crypto Twitter itself. Traders complain about lower price ceilings on tokens, he says, while too few people build protocols that could change that.

Ansem. Source: X

His optimism on select tokens matches his August call, when Ansem predicted that Pump.fun's token could join crypto's top 10 by 2028.

For now, Ansem is bearish on Bitcoin but still sees room for some onchain projects. In his view, tokens will only break through lower price ceilings if builders put in the work to ship protocols worth owning.

"I am shocked, absolutely shocked, that Anthropic ARR has likely gone vertical in October after they cut token prices. Except the exact same thing happened for the entire AI market, which is why GPU rental prices have surged while token prices declined," Gavin Baker, managing partner at investment firm Atreides Management, said in a sarcastic X post.

He said Anthropic could achieve a $100 billion annualized recurring revenue (ARR) rate by the year's end.

Investment professionals specifically praised its customer base and expansion potential.

Creative Strategies CEO Ben Bajarin said more than half of Fortune 500 companies already qualify as significant Anthropic customers, but the revenue from them averages less than 0.1% of their expenses.

"Its ten largest Fortune 500 customers spend more than eight times the cohort average, yet still allocate less than 1% of their expenses to Anthropic," Bajarin wrote, suggesting room for getting those customers to spend more on Anthropic's AI technology.

Daniel McCarthy, a marketing professor at Robert H. Smith School of Business, University of Maryland, praised Anthropic's financial performance and said that falling AI inference costs supports its path to profitability.

"So in sum, explosive growth. Lots of customers. Great funnel. Mostly B2B. Lots of revenue expansion in B2B. Next is ofc "how are margins?". The S-1 was a strong +ive datapoint for me," McCarthy said in a LinkedIn post.

"Yes, their stated loss is $80.7B for the first half of 2026, but all of that loss is from noncash fair value changes on convertible notes, SAFEs, etc. The company got more valuable, so the paper it issued got more expensive. When you look at the OPERATING business, they were GAAP profitable on an operating basis in Q2, [with an] 8.4% GAAP operating margin. 85.4% gross margin (some caveats here, nothing fatal)! The business is profitable when it's utilized. Cost per token is going down quickly," he wrote.

QQQ and QQQM track the identical Nasdaq-100 Index, but QQQM charges 0.15% versus QQQ's 0.18%, saving $30 annually on a $100,000 balance.

Invesco, which manages both funds, cut QQQ's expense ratio from 0.20% to 0.18% in December 2025 after shareholders approved a structural reclassification.

One Index, One Sponsor, Two Price Tags

Both funds' prospectuses name the Nasdaq-100 Index as the underlying index. QQQ's prospectus says the fund tries to track the index's investment results, before fees and expenses. It describes the index as 100 of the largest domestic and international non-financial companies listed on U.S. Nasdaq-affiliated listing exchanges based on market capitalization. QQQ uses full replication, which means it holds every index security at its index weight.

The two funds are tied together on paper. When the index methodology changed on May 1, 2026, Invesco amended both prospectuses in a single supplement dated April 30, 2026.
